Radio

A native radio group: exactly one of a few options, each with room for a full label and a description, sent with a form.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • To choose exactly one of two to six options that need a full label or a line of description each.
  • When the reader should see every option before choosing.

When not to use it

  • For two to five options with one- or two-word labels. Use a segmented control.
  • For more than six options. Use a select.
  • For options where any number may be chosen. Use checkboxes.
  • For a single on-or-off setting. Use a switch, or a checkbox inside a form.

Accessibility

  • Use a fieldset with gw-radio__group and a legend with gw-radio__legend that asks the question. Each option is a div with gw-radio holding input type="radio" with gw-radio__input, then a label with gw-radio__label whose for attribute is the input's id.
  • Every input in a group has the same name attribute, and a different name from every other group on the page.
  • The options are one above the other. The input comes first in each row: the stylesheet reads its state to style the label after it.
  • A description is a p with gw-radio__description, linked from its input with aria-describedby.
  • Disable one option with the disabled attribute on its input, or the whole group with disabled on the fieldset. Say why in a description.
  • For an error, the fieldset takes role="radiogroup", aria-labelledby pointing at the legend, aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at a p with gw-radio__error after the last option. The message says what to do, and its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
  • Tab moves into the group, to the chosen option or the first one. The arrow keys move between options and choose as they go, and Space chooses the focused option. All of it comes from the native inputs.
  • The circle is drawn 20px across and its pointer target is 44px; a press on the label chooses the option too.
